messages:
Maya (CSM): Quick weekly check-in for Helio Corp — hosted API spend vs commit. Week-over-week usage +34%. We're at ~68% of the monthly commit. Two anomaly flags yesterday: sudden token surge (03/19 14:22 UTC) and a short series of 500s in eu-west-1. Posting the skinny so we can agree next steps.

billing-bot: Automated report: `commit_monthly: $30,000; month_to_date_spend: $20,350; projected_end_of_month_spend (linear): $29,100; active_api_keys: 12; top3_callers: service-frontend (46%), ingestion-worker (28%), analytics-batch (9%)`

Jules (Finance): Thanks. Projected looks within commit but margin is small. Do we know if that token surge is legitimate traffic or a noisy job?

Maya (CSM): Early look: two contributors — a feature flag rollout from Helio devs (frontend floods some batch endpoints) + one misconfigured cron that retried on 429s. I flagged the cron.

telemetry-bot: Error summary (last 6h): `5xx_rate_eu-west-1: 0.8% -> spike to 3.9% during 14:20-14:45 UTC; avg_latency_p95_eu-west-1: 420ms -> 1.2s during spike; token_rate_per_minute: baseline 2.1k -> peak 7.6k`

Ravi (AE): Is Helio on a self-serve plan or are they in a reserved commit with monthly true-ups? Need to know how aggressive we are on nudging a commit increase.

Jules (Finance): They're on a hosted monthly commit ($30k) with standard overage policy. We prefer to avoid surprise overages. If trend keeps, they could be close to the commit but still under it.

Maya (CSM): Agreed. Short-term ops: 1) I asked Helio to rollback the feature flag for the next hour. 2) Sam, can you run a quick onboarding playbook to walk them through recommended batching/caching? 3) We should set a soft quota on the ingestion-worker key to avoid a repeat accidental loop.

Sam (Onboarding): On it. I'll schedule a 30-min enablement today (timezone permitting) and share a minimal batching/caching snippet. Also will check for any SDK retries that might be amplifying traffic.

Maya (CSM): I'll open a support ticket for the 500s and attach relevant traces. If billing-team agrees, propose a temporary burst window for this month to avoid friction while they stabilize.

Jules (Finance): Temporary burst policy is OK if Helio agrees to tighter observability and an enablement session. But we should capture acceptance in email.

Ravi (AE): I'll ping Helio exec and suggest the enablement + confirm they want to keep current commit or discuss bump. I'll also ask for the PR/feature rollout owner so we can align throttles.

Maya (CSM): TL;DR action items: - Maya: open support ticket + traces (done) - Sam: enablement + SDK retry audit - Billing: prepare temporary burst proposal text for customer - Ravi: coordinate with Helio on rollout owner and confirm acceptance

billing-bot: Billing note: `current_commit_utilization: 68%; safe_buffer: ~$900; if weekly runrate from last 48h continues, projection: +3% over commit by month end`

Jules (Finance): Ok — please add the burst proposal to the ticket and cc me. If they want to increase commit, we can fast-track a quarter-term amendment.

Maya (CSM): One more ask — can infra add a per-key soft throttle suggestion for customers who hit >3x baseline bursts? That would cut noisy spikes early. @telemetry-bot any quick config suggestion?

telemetry-bot: Suggestion: `soft_throttle_window: 60s; throttle_threshold: 3x baseline; action: emit warning+429 for 30s then allow graceful ramp`. We can push a runbook snippet to the ticket.

Sam (Onboarding): I'll include that snippet in the enablement deck. Also will recommend KV prefix caching for the analytics-batch flows.

Ravi (AE): Customer response: they acknowledged the rollback and asked for the enablement invite. They want to avoid changing commit for now if we can guarantee a short burst protection.

Maya (CSM): Great — moving to 'working' on the ticket. I'll follow up after the enablement with a short readout and whether finance needs to propose commit changes. For now, tagging this as medium renewal risk until the enablement happens. :eyes:

Jules (Finance): Noted. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:
